questions.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+3y=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt+2\operatorname{sin}⁡pt,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=3\,⟹\,\omega =\sqrt{3}.
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{3}t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{3}t.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency $p$ of the external periodic force $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡pt+2\operatorname{sin}⁡pt$ coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega =\sqrt{3}.$

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when $p=\sqrt{3}.$

questions.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+18y=6{sin}^{2}⁡pt,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=18\,⟹\,\omega =3\sqrt{2}.
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\sqrt{2}t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\sqrt{2}t).
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=6{sin}^{2}⁡pt$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega =3\sqrt{2}.$ Since 

$$
f(t)=6{sin}^{2}⁡pt=3-3\operatorname{cos}⁡2pt,
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $2p.$

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when $p=\frac{\omega }{2}=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.$

questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.8\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force 

$$
F(t)=(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-2)\,\text{N}
$$

is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.8{y}^{″}=-ky+(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-2).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5k}{4}y=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=\frac{5k}{4}\,⟹\,k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1)$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$ Since

$$
f(t)=\frac{5}{2}(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{5}{2}t)-1)=\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t),
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $5.$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{4}{5}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{4}{5}\cdot {5}^{2}=20\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.5\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force 

$$
F(t)=2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)\,\text{N}
$$

is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.5{y}^{″}=-ky+2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+2ky=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=2k\,⟹\,k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$ Since

$$
f(t)=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)=2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)),
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $4.$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {4}^{2}=8\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $3.$ Therefore,
$\omega =3.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =3$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(6D-9Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-(6C+9Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)]+9t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ 6D\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-6C\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & =10\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=0$ and $D=\frac{5}{3}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{5}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Solutions I, II, and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".
